data.name: Metal Drift
data.detailed_description:
Metal Drift is a vehicular sport combat game set in a distant future. As the player, you command an agile, high powered hover tank in a futuristic sports arena. Core game play centers on intense tank-on-tank multiplayer team combat seen through an immersive, first person cockpit. Layered on this is a goal-oriented game type that allows for high level strategy and team dynamics. Players can level up to unlock new ranks, weapons, and upgrades.
Each weapon and upgrade is specifically designed and balanced to allow different styles of play. Pair up the Stealth upgrade and the Shock Cannon to uncloak behind an enemy player and unload a devastating blow before disappearing again. Or choose the Sensor upgrade to see where all the nearby players are, and the Temporal Cannon to shoot them through walls! There are 56 possible combinations – choose whichever suits your strategy.
  • Multiplayer team-based vehicular combat
  • 5 Different arenas featuring multiple levels and boost tunnels
  • Persistent leveling system – level-up to unlock new weapons and upgrades
  • Stats and Leaderboards
  • 56 Different tank configurations
  • 18 Steam Achievements, with more coming soon!
  • Unique energy management system – accumulate energy and then distribute it to weapons or use it to gain a speed boost!

reviews.review:
Metal Drift offers an unusual combination of futuristic vehicular combat and competitive team sports, delivering an experience that stands apart from conventional multiplayer shooters. Developed and published by Black Jacket Studios, this arena-based action game places players inside heavily armed hover tanks and challenges them to combine precise shooting, rapid movement, and tactical cooperation. Instead of focusing exclusively on eliminating opponents, matches revolve around capturing a ball and delivering it into the opposing team's goal. This distinctive objective transforms ordinary combat into a strategic contest where teamwork, positioning, and quick decisions matter just as much as firepower. Although the game shows its age in several areas, its inventive mechanics provide a compelling foundation for players who appreciate unconventional competitive experiences.

The core gameplay is built around fast-paced matches involving two opposing teams, with support for up to twelve players. Controlling a hover tank from a first-person perspective creates a satisfying sense of speed and mechanical power. Players must constantly balance attacking enemies, defending teammates, intercepting opponents, and advancing toward the enemy goal. Unlike traditional deathmatch shooters, destroying another tank does not automatically translate into victory. Success requires understanding the objective and coordinating movements with teammates. This approach makes matches particularly entertaining when both teams employ organized strategies, although newcomers may initially struggle with the combination of navigation, combat, and objective management.

Movement is among the game's most enjoyable features. Hover tanks can navigate complex arenas, exploit elevated pathways, and accelerate through designated boost tunnels. The ability to maneuver quickly across the battlefield gives encounters an energetic rhythm, while vertical environments encourage players to think beyond straightforward attacks. Learning the layout of each arena becomes increasingly important because effective positioning can determine whether an offensive push succeeds or fails. The first-person cockpit presentation enhances immersion, although it occasionally makes tracking nearby opponents and judging spatial relationships more difficult than in third-person vehicular games.

Another interesting mechanic involves managing energy between weapons and movement. Players must decide whether to spend resources on offensive attacks or preserve them for acceleration and tactical repositioning. This creates meaningful decisions during combat, particularly when chasing a ball carrier or escaping an unfavorable confrontation. Aggressive players may prefer maximizing damage output, while more defensive competitors can benefit from conserving energy for timely interceptions. The system is accessible enough to understand quickly but offers additional depth as players become familiar with different combat situations.

Customization adds considerable variety through 56 possible tank configurations involving weapons and upgrades. Different equipment combinations support aggressive assaults, stealth-oriented tactics, and specialized defensive approaches. Experimenting with these configurations encourages players to develop their preferred combat style while adapting to opposing strategies. A persistent progression system further rewards participation by unlocking additional equipment and ranks. However, this structure can create an uneven experience when newcomers encounter veterans with broader customization options. Although skill and teamwork remain essential, the progression system may occasionally make competitive encounters feel less balanced.

The game features five arenas designed around interconnected routes, multiple elevations, and opportunities for tactical movement. Their layouts complement the hover-tank mechanics by encouraging flanking maneuvers, defensive positioning, and rapid transitions between offensive and defensive roles. While the environments provide enough complexity to reward practice, their limited number eventually becomes noticeable. Additional maps, alternative objectives, and more varied competitive modes could have significantly improved long-term replayability. Nevertheless, the existing arenas successfully support the central gameplay concept.

Visually, Metal Drift carries the unmistakable appearance of an older independent PC release. Its science-fiction environments, mechanical vehicles, and weapon effects establish an appropriate atmosphere, but the graphical presentation lacks the detail and refinement expected from modern competitive games. Environmental textures and geometric structures appear relatively basic, while visual effects prioritize functionality over spectacle. The sound design contributes to the sensation of futuristic combat without becoming particularly memorable. Fortunately, the relatively straightforward presentation helps maintain battlefield readability, allowing players to concentrate on movement and tactical decisions rather than elaborate visual distractions.

Single-player matches against computer-controlled opponents provide an opportunity to practice movement, experiment with equipment, and understand the objectives before competing against human players. However, artificial intelligence cannot consistently reproduce the unpredictability and coordinated strategies that make multiplayer matches exciting. The game's dependence on an active community is therefore a significant concern. Finding enough participants for competitive matches may be difficult, and playing exclusively against bots diminishes some of the experience's greatest strengths. Organizing private matches with friends is likely the most rewarding way to appreciate its mechanics today.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently classified as Unknown, meaning there is no confirmed official Valve verification establishing reliable handheld functionality. Because Metal Drift was designed primarily for older Windows systems, running it through SteamOS may require Proton adjustments or customized controls. Its modest hardware demands are encouraging, but they do not guarantee successful operation. Players seeking a dependable handheld experience should consider this uncertainty before purchasing.

Overall, Metal Drift remains an imaginative multiplayer action game with satisfying movement, engaging energy management, and a distinctive combination of armored combat and competitive sports. Its mechanical creativity deserves appreciation, even though its limited content, dated presentation, progression imbalance, and uncertain multiplayer activity restrict its appeal today. For enthusiasts of experimental arena shooters or groups seeking an unusual competitive experience, it still offers worthwhile entertainment.

Metal Drift is a creative and mechanically rewarding arena combat game whose strongest ideas remain appealing despite its age. Its combination of teamwork, customization, and high-speed vehicular action makes it worth considering for players who enjoy unconventional multiplayer games, provided its online functionality is accessible.

Rating: 6/10
